title: Cross-sector CERT bodies issue joint AI-found embedded-CVE guidance by Q3 2027
body: By Q3 2027 at least four sector-specific cybersecurity authorities — CISA (industrial control systems), the FDA Center for Devices and Radiological Health (medical devices), NHTSA's Office of Vehicle Safety Research (automotive), and ENISA's transport-sector unit (covering the EU Cyber Resilience Act perimeter) — publish coordinated disclosure and remediation guidance explicitly naming AI-discovered vulnerabilities in shared cryptographic libraries embedded across IoT, automotive, and industrial-control device fleets, with wolfSSL CVE-2026-5194 (CVSS 9.1, certificate-forgery flaw in a TLS library Anthropic's Project Glasswing surfaced inside roughly five billion devices) cited as the reference case. The cross-sectoral coordination problem is structural: a single AI-discovered cryptographic flaw lands simultaneously inside infusion pumps (FDA jurisdiction), vehicle telematics units (NHTSA), grid-edge SCADA controllers (CISA), and rail/aviation signalling (TSA / ENISA transport) — and each sectoral regulator currently runs its own disclosure cadence, its own remediation SLA, and its own software-bill-of-materials format. Project Glasswing's 10,000+ findings cohort and the 530 high/critical maintainer disclosures it has already moved through the embargo pipeline force the question: when one AI run produces a five-billion-device exposure across four sectoral regimes inside a single CVE, can a sector-by-sector response actually mitigate the cascade in time. The forcing function is mechanical — the EU Cyber Resilience Act's manufacturer obligations come into force across 2027, the FDA's pre-market and post-market cybersecurity guidance is on a 2027 refresh cycle following the 2024 final guidance, and CISA's Secure by Design pledge program will have absorbed at least two more AI-found embedded-CVE waves by the end of Q1 2027 if the Glasswing cadence holds. Expect the coordinated guidance to land via a memorandum of understanding or joint advisory between the named authorities (CISA-FDA-NHTSA-ENISA at minimum), specifying a uniform SBOM disclosure format for AI-found vulnerabilities in shared dependencies, a tiered remediation SLA keyed to device-population scale and operational-criticality, and a named coordination point of contact at the frontier lab that ran the scan. The bear case is that CISA and ENISA ship parallel but unreconciled guidance, with FDA and NHTSA each waiting for the other sector to publish first, slipping the four-way coordinated document into 2028; absent that fragmentation, Q3 2027 lands the first cross-sector coordinated guidance naming AI-discovered embedded vulnerabilities as a distinct disclosure class.

reasoning.because: wolfSSL CVE-2026-5194 (CVSS 9.1) hits ~5B IoT/automotive/ICS devices across four sectoral regimes
reasoning.given: EU CRA 2027 in-force date + FDA 2027 cyber guidance refresh + CISA Secure by Design pledge
reasoning.so_that: CISA, FDA, NHTSA, ENISA publish joint disclosure-and-remediation guidance naming AI-found embedded CVEs
reasoning.landing: Q3 2027; four-authority MoU or joint advisory with uniform SBOM + tiered SLA
reasoning.plain_language: One AI scan just found a bug in software used in five billion devices, so safety agencies will write shared rules together by 2027.

summary: wolfSSL CVE-2026-5194 (CVSS 9.1), the certificate-forgery flaw Project Glasswing surfaced, landed inside ~5B IoT, automotive, and industrial-control devices spanning four sectoral regimes at once. By Q3 2027 CISA, FDA, NHTSA, and ENISA publish joint guidance naming AI-found embedded CVEs.
